findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "start_test" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Start the Typeza personality test in this conversation: 41 short questions, no account needed. Returns draft_id and key (keep both and pass them back unchanged)…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description tells the model to hide behavior

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "list_my_people" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_my_invite_link, list_my_people · Private data: choose_test_type · Public sink: answer_test, get_my_invite_link, list_my_people.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_my_invite_link, list_my_people · Private data: choose_test_type · Public sink: answer_test, get_my_invite_link, list_my_people

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

detail: Tool "get_relationship_between" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
